q: Château Musar's long-lived Cabernet-Cinsault-Carignan blend comes from which valley?
exp: Made through civil war; released seven years after vintage.

q: Giuseppe Quintarelli's cheaper 'declassified' Amarone-method red is labeled:
exp: Rosso del Bepi appears when Amarone isn't declared; Alzero is the Cabernet Franc amarone-style rarity.

q: Which Napa winery won the 1976 Paris tasting for Chardonnay, under winemaker Miljenko 'Mike' Grgich?
exp: Grgich later founded Grgich Hills; the red winner was Stag's Leap Wine Cellars '73.

q: Name Guigal's three single-vineyard Côte-Rôties, the slope each sits on, and which is one hundred per cent Syrah.
accept: la mouline la turque and la landonne with landonne pure syrah
mouline is cote blonde with viognier landonne is cote brune and pure syrah
la landonne is one hundred per cent syrah and la mouline has the most viognier
the three la las are mouline turque and landonne
ans: La Mouline on the Côte Blonde, with the largest Viognier share at around eleven per cent; La Turque on the Côte Brune side with a smaller Viognier component, roughly five to seven per cent; and La Landonne on the Côte Brune, one hundred per cent Syrah and the most tannic and slowest of the three. Each is raised around forty-two months in new oak.
exp: The slopes explain the wines: the Côte Blonde is lighter, sandier granitic-schist soil and gives perfume, while the iron-rich schist and clay of the Côte Brune gives structure and iron. First vintages are La Mouline 1966, La Landonne 1978 and La Turque 1985, the last arriving with Guigal's purchase of Vidal-Fleury. The fourth bottling to know is Château d'Ampuis, first made in 1995 from seven lieux-dits — the blend that sits just below the La Las and is the sane way onto the list.

q: Krug bottles two walled single vineyards. Name them, their villages and their grapes.
accept: clos du mesnil is chardonnay and clos d'ambonnay is pinot noir
clos du mesnil at le mesnil sur oger and clos d'ambonnay at ambonnay
krug's two walled vineyards are mesnil chardonnay and ambonnay pinot noir
ans: Clos du Mesnil — 1.84 hectares of Chardonnay inside a wall at Le Mesnil-sur-Oger on the Côte des Blancs, first vintage 1979. And Clos d'Ambonnay — about 0.68 hectares of Pinot Noir at Ambonnay in the Montagne de Reims, first vintage 1995, released in 2007 and among the most expensive Champagnes made.
exp: The clos bottlings are the exception that proves the house doctrine rather than a contradiction of it. Krug's identity is assemblage — Grande Cuvée blends well over a hundred wines across more than ten vintages — and the family's argument is that these two exist only because a wall makes them genuinely distinct, not because Krug believes single sites outrank blending. The Clos du Mesnil wall dates from 1698, which is the detail examiners like.

q: Which Loire grower turned Sauvignon Blanc into a collectible, from which appellation, and name two of his cuvées.
accept: didier dagueneau in pouilly-fume with silex and pur sang
dagueneau pouilly fume silex pur sang buisson renard
didier dagueneau died in 2008 and louis-benjamin continues the domaine
ans: Didier Dagueneau, in Pouilly-Fumé — Silex and Pur Sang above all, with Buisson Renard and the entry Blanc Fumé de Pouilly beneath them; he also made a Sancerre from Chavignol's Mont Damné and a sweet Jurançon, Les Jardins de Babylone. He died in a light-aircraft crash in 2008, and his children Louis-Benjamin and Charlotte have run the domaine since without a drop in standard.
exp: He is the reason a serious list can carry Sauvignon Blanc at three figures: brutally low yields, ploughing by horse, late picking and ageing in oak including cigar-shaped foudres, aimed squarely at an appellation he thought lazy. Watch the trap in the names — Silex and Pur Sang are cuvées, not classified vineyards, even though Silex takes its name from the flint soils. Pair him with Vatan or Cotat in Sancerre when an examiner asks who else farms at that level.

q: G-Max, the most sought-after dry German Riesling of the modern era, comes from:
exp: Klaus-Peter Keller at Flörsheim-Dalsheim, first vintage 2001, the name assembled from his grandfather Georg and his son Maximilian. The source parcel has deliberately never been disclosed, which is part of the mystique and also why G-Max carries no Grosses Gewächs vineyard name. Keller's named wines to hold alongside it are Hubacker, Abtserde and Morstein. The distractors are wrong on style as well as address: Prüm is the Mosel's reference for delicate, sweet Prädikat wine, and both Nahe estates are known for aromatic precision rather than for a cult dry bottling.

q: Name Côte-Rôtie's two fabled slopes and the family metaphor attached.
ans: Côte Brune and Côte Blonde — the lord of Maugiron's dark- and fair-haired daughters
exp: Brune: schist and iron, sterner wine; Blonde: gneiss-granite, silkier.

q: Which single-vineyard Côte-Rôtie does Guigal bottle alongside La Mouline and La Landonne?
Which northern Rhône cru grows on the steep granite amphitheater once terraced by Rome, permits only Syrah, and forbids white grapes entirely?
exp: Clape, Allemand, Verset — black wine of granite; Saint-Péray next door is whites-only.

q: Hermitage's most famous single climats include Les Bessards, Le Méal and:
ans: L'Ermite (also Les Greffieux; Chapoutier bottles all as selections parcellaires)
exp: Bessards' granite gives the spine; Chave blends across climats on principle.

q: What is 'vin de paille' in Hermitage?
ans: A rare straw wine from dried Marsanne/Roussanne
exp: Chave and Chapoutier revive it in great years.

q: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's founding regulations of 1936 were drafted largely by which figure?
ans: Baron Pierre Le Roy de Boiseaumarié (Château Fortia)
exp: The prototype for all French AOC law, with Joseph Capus.

q: The modern cahier des charges enumerates Châteauneuf-du-Pape's permitted varieties with each colour variant listed separately. How many does that make?
exp: The cahier des charges enumerates 18 once the colour variants are counted separately (Grenache noir/gris/blanc, Clairette blanche/rose, Piquepoul noir/gris/blanc, Terret noir); 13 is the count by variety name — the figure behind 'Beaucastel plants all thirteen'. This question is keyed to the decree's 18.

q: Château Rayas' singularity among Châteauneuf estates lies in:
ans: Essentially 100% Grenache from cool, sandy, galet-free pinewood parcels

q: Which southern Rhône villages were promoted out of Côtes-du-Rhône Villages to cru status in the 2005–2016 era? Name at least two, with their years.
ans: e.g., Vinsobres (2006), Rasteau (2010, dry reds), Cairanne (2016)
exp: The cru ladder keeps lengthening; Beaumes-de-Venise reds rose in 2005.
